_meta.description: Canonical CR (Change Request) lifecycle schema for the AITeamForge kanban system. v2.0 adds the CR-as-Container pattern: a top-level crs[] collection (mirrors epics[]/releases[]) and a crAssignment back-pointer on items (mirrors releaseAssignment). Per-item cr_* fields are deprecated but retained for migration compatibility.
consumers: migrate-cr-schema.py — reads crStates/crFields/teamConfig/crContainer to patch team boards
scripts/kb-cr.sh — reads crStates for valid transition targets and field names
lcars-ui/server.py — reads teamConfig.crSupport.enabled to gate CR endpoints
critical_invariants: Cycle-time fields listed in crDerived MUST NOT be persisted to board JSON.
They are computed at read time from crTimestamps values.
teamConfig.crSupport.enabled defaults to false. kb-cr helpers no-op silently when false.
Do NOT store cr_cycle_*_days or deploy_estimate_delta_days in any board or item.

Per-item cr_* fields (crFields section) are DEPRECATED as of schema v2.0. They remain in the schema ONLY so migrate-cr-schema.py can read and transform them. Remove after all boards have been migrated.
New CRs must be created as crs[] container records. crAssignment.crId on the item points to the parent CR record.
'cr-drafted' semantically means: the CR markdown has been published to Confluence as a request page. The CR-Proper page does NOT yet exist.
'cr-submitted' semantically means: a CR-Proper page link has been appended to the bottom of the request page. The poller (XACA-0328-003) detects this link and writes cr_proper_url.

'cr-closed' semantically means: the CR has been manually archived and is no longer active. This is a terminal state reachable from any other state via kb-cr close. It does NOT increment pushback_count — it is a neutral archive operation, not a rejection. cr-closed CRs are excluded from default list/filter views to keep dashboards clean.

crContainer._description: Schema for a CR container record stored in the top-level crs[] array on the board. Mirrors the epics[]/releases[] pattern. Each CR record is the authoritative source for its lifecycle state and timestamps. Items link to a CR via crAssignment.crId.

id.description: Unique CR identifier. Format: CR-<TEAM_UPPER>-<YYYYMMDD>-<seq> (e.g., CR-IOS-20260515-0123). Generated by kb-cr draft.

title.description: Short human-readable title for the CR. Defaults to the parent kanban item title when drafted from a single item.

type.description: CR classification. 'major' requires CAB approval; 'emergency' bypasses CAB with mandatory justification; 'fyi' is informational only.

crState.description: Current CR lifecycle state. Must be a value from the crStates array. Transitions are managed exclusively by kb-cr subcommands.

deploy_window_planned.description: Planned deployment window start (e.g., 2026-05-15T22:00:00Z). Immutable once submitted to prevent scope drift after CAB review begins.

cr_doc_link.description: Path or URL to the full CR markdown document (e.g., kanban/plans/XIOS-0123/CR.md or a Confluence URL).

cr_proper_url.description: URL of the appended CR-Proper Confluence page link discovered at the bottom of the CR request page. Presence indicates the CR has been formally submitted (cr-submitted). Populated by the Confluence poller daemon (XACA-0328-003) when the link is detected. Manual entry via the LCARS state-change UI (XACA-0328-004) is also permitted.

approver.description: Approver identity. Populated by kb-cr approve.

login.description: Login/handle of the approver (e.g., GitHub username or Jira account ID).

name.description: Human-readable display name of the approver.

itemIds.description: Ordered list of kanban item IDs covered by this CR. A CR may span multiple items (e.g., a cross-platform deploy). Items point back via crAssignment.crId.

pushback_count.description: Number of times this CR has been returned for rework. Incremented automatically on each rejection.

pushback_notes.description: Cumulative CAB reviewer notes explaining pushback reasons. Appended (not replaced) on each rejection.

summary.description: One-paragraph plain-language summary of what this CR changes and why. Targeted at non-technical CAB reviewers.

platform.description: Target deployment platform. Used by LCARS to route CR notifications and filter board views.

emergency_justification.description: Mandatory justification text when type is 'emergency'. Explains why normal CAB review is being bypassed.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the CR container record was created (kb-cr draft).

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent state transition or field update on this CR record.

timestamps.description: All lifecycle timestamps for this CR record. Mirrors crTimestamps but stored on the container, not the item.

crAssignment._description: Back-pointer object added to each kanban item that belongs to a CR container. Mirrors the releaseAssignment pattern: {releaseId, releaseName, platform, assignedAt}. This is the ONLY CR linkage field on the item after migration — all lifecycle state and timestamps move to the crs[] container record.

crId.description: ID of the parent CR container record in the crs[] array (e.g., CR-IOS-20260515-0123).

crTitle.description: Snapshot of the CR title at assignment time. Denormalized for display without a crs[] lookup.

assignedAt.description: Timestamp when this item was assigned to the CR container.

crFields._deprecated: DEPRECATED as of schema v2.0. These per-item fields are superseded by the crs[] container + crAssignment back-pointer pattern. They are retained here ONLY so migrate-cr-schema.py can read and transform existing board data. DO NOT write new per-item cr_* fields. Remove this section after all boards have been migrated and verified.

cr_id.description: DEPRECATED. Use crs[].id + crAssignment.crId instead. Unique CR identifier, assigned at draft time. Format: CR-<TEAM>-<YYYYMMDD>-<seq>.

cr_type.description: DEPRECATED. Use crs[].type instead. CR classification. Required at draft time.

crTimestamps._description: Lifecycle timestamps recorded on the CR container record (crs[] entry). In schema v2.0 these live on the container, not on individual items. Per-item cr_*_at fields (listed in crFields) are deprecated.

cr_testing_started_at.recorded_when: kb-cr start-test is called (does not change crState; item status field tracks testing)

cr_completed_at.recorded_when: kb-cr complete is called; item also moves to completed status via kb-done

crDerived._warning: These fields are computed at READ TIME from crTimestamps. They MUST NOT be stored in board JSON or item records. Writing them to disk is a schema violation.

cr_cycle_draft_to_submit_days.description: Time from CR draft to CAB submission. Measures how long preparation took.

cr_cycle_submit_to_approve_days.description: CAB review cycle time. Measures how quickly the board approves or returns CRs.

cr_cycle_approve_to_dev_days.description: Time from approval to dev start. Detects scheduling friction or queue buildup.

cr_cycle_dev_to_test_days.description: Development duration. Time from dev start to handoff for testing.

cr_cycle_deploydev_to_deployprod_days.description: Soak time between dev and prod deployments.

cr_cycle_total_days.description: End-to-end CR lifecycle duration from draft to completion.

deploy_estimate_delta_days.formula: (cr_deployed_prod_at - deploy_window_planned) in fractional days; negative = early, positive = late
deploy_estimate_delta_days.description: Variance between planned and actual prod deployment. Negative values mean early delivery; positive means late.

crSupport.description: Load-bearing feature flag. When false (the default), ALL kb-cr subcommands exit 0 with a single informational message and perform NO side effects — no board reads, no writes, no state transitions. This is the primary isolation mechanism preventing CR schema fields from leaking into teams that have not opted in. Set to true ONLY after running migrate-cr-schema.py against the team's board and confirming the crStates array is present. Configure via SETTINGS → TEAM CONFIG → 'Enable CR (CAB) support' in the LCARS UI.

boardFields._description: Top-level board fields added by migrate-cr-schema.py when crSupport is enabled. Mirrors the nextEpicId / nextReleaseId pattern for ID generation.

crs.description: Top-level collection of CR container records. Each entry conforms to the crContainer schema above. Indexed by crs[].id. Managed exclusively by kb-cr subcommands.

nextCrSeq.description: Auto-incrementing sequence counter for CR ID generation. kb-cr draft reads this, generates CR-<TEAM>-<YYYYMMDD>-<nextCrSeq>, then increments and writes back. Mirrors nextEpicId / nextReleaseId.
